\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ترام} (trām)}{ترام (trām)}]{\ar{ترام} (trām) — a tram}

\label{lesson:AR-C445-tram}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an adapter, then the Arabic for to light up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ترام}}
\textbf{\ar{ترام}} — \emph{trām} — \textquotedblleft{}a tram\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ركبنا} \ar{الترام} \ar{إلى} \ar{وسط} \ar{المدينة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rakibnā at-trām ilā wasaṭ al-madīna.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We took the tram to the city centre.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ترام}} (\emph{trām}) is usually traced to English \emph{tram}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{trām}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{trām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rakibnā at-trām ilā wasaṭ al-madīna.} — We took the tram to the city centre.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an adapter, then the Arabic for to light up, then say \emph{trām} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ترام} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A tram\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شاحنة} (shāḥina)}{شاحنة (shāḥina)}]{\ar{شاحنة} (shāḥina) — a lorry; a truck}

\label{lesson:AR-C445-shahina}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to light up, then the Arabic for a tram.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شاحنة}}
\textbf{\ar{شاحنة}} — \emph{shāḥina} — \textquotedblleft{}a lorry; a truck\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وقفت} \ar{شاحنة} \ar{كبيرة} \ar{في} \ar{وسط} \ar{الطريق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{waqafat shāḥina kabīra fī wasaṭ aṭ-ṭarīq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A big lorry stopped in the middle of the road.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شاحنة}} (\emph{shāḥina}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-ḥ-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to load (a ship)\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is an active participle: the vehicle that carries loads; \emph{shāḥin}, \textquotedblleft{}a charger\textquotedblright{}, shares the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shāḥina}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shāḥina}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waqafat shāḥina kabīra fī wasaṭ aṭ-ṭarīq.} — A big lorry stopped in the middle of the road.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to light up, then the Arabic for a tram, then say \emph{shāḥina} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شاحنة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A lorry; a truck\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مقود} (miqwad)}{مقود (miqwad)}]{\ar{مقود} (miqwad) — a steering wheel}

\label{lesson:AR-C445-miqwad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a tram, then the Arabic for a lorry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مقود}}
\textbf{\ar{مقود}} — \emph{miqwad} — \textquotedblleft{}a steering wheel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أمسك} \ar{أبي} \ar{المقود} \ar{بقوة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{amsaka abī al-miqwad bi-quwwa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father held the steering wheel tightly.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مقود}} (\emph{miqwad}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-w-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to lead\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The tool pattern \emph{mifʿal} makes it the thing one steers with.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{miqwad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amsaka abī al-miqwad bi-quwwa.} — My father held the steering wheel tightly.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a tram, then the Arabic for a lorry, then say \emph{miqwad} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تمهل} (tamahhala)}{تمهل (tamahhala)}]{\ar{تمهل} (tamahhala) — to slow down; to take one's time}

\label{lesson:AR-C445-tamahhala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a lorry, then the Arabic for a steering wheel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تمهل}}
\textbf{\ar{تمهل}} — \emph{tamahhala} — \textquotedblleft{}to slow down; to take one's time\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تمهل} \ar{أبي} \ar{عند} \ar{المنعطف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tamahhala abī ʿinda al-munʿaṭaf.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father slowed down at the bend.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتمهل}, \emph{yatamahhal}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تمهل}} (\emph{tamahhala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-h-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to act gently, without haste\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a lorry, then the Arabic for a steering wheel, then say \emph{tamahhala} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عرقل} (ʿarqala)}{عرقل (ʿarqala)}]{\ar{عرقل} (ʿarqala) — to hamper; to hold up}

\label{lesson:AR-C445-arqala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a steering wheel, then the Arabic for to slow down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عرقل}}
\textbf{\ar{عرقل}} — \emph{ʿarqala} — \textquotedblleft{}to hamper; to hold up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عرقل} \ar{الثلج} \ar{حركة} \ar{المرور}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿarqala ath-thalj ḥarakat al-murūr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The snow held up the traffic.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعرقل}, \emph{yuʿarqil}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عرقل}} (\emph{ʿarqala}) is a verb with four root letters; the origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
